Five of the Magnificent Seven, Including Tesla and Amazon, Push Back on OKX-ICE Stock Tokenization; Number of Objecting Companies Rises to 56
sum: Major listed companies are mounting a collective pushback against the stock tokenization project pursued by OKXICE, a joint venture between Intercontinental Exchange (ICE)—the parent of the New York Stock Exchange—and crypto exchange OKX. According to an OKXICE notice published on the 3rd (local time), 56 of the 62 target companies have filed objections. Among them, six companies—Tesla, Amazon, SpaceX, Netflix, Lam Research and SoFi Technologies—newly expressed their opposition in this round.

In particular, five of the six Magnificent Seven (M7) members other than Apple have joined the opposition: Nvidia, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Tesla. Apple is the only M7 company that has not objected. Broadcom, Qualcomm, Oracle, Intel, Micron, AMD, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, McDonald's, Coca-Cola, Walmart and Eli Lilly also appear on the objection list.

The objections are grounded in an innovation exemption issued by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in September. The exemption allows exchanges such as OKXICE to handle tokenized U.S. stocks without registering as formal exchanges, while also granting companies the right to object to third-party tokenization of their shares. OKXICE issued its first notice on the 4th of last month, after which a 30-day objection window was granted; that deadline fell on this day.

Stock tokenization is a method of representing assets or rights linked to physical shares as blockchain-based digital tokens. It has drawn interest from the global financial industry because it enables fractional trading and 24-hour trading. However, a key point of contention is that token holders do not receive shareholder rights such as ownership or voting rights guaranteed by the underlying shares.

The companies that newly objected did not disclose specific reasons. Industry observers, however, see the backdrop as the difficulty issuers face in tracking shareholder composition or the channels for delivering voting rights and dividends when third parties tokenize their shares without consent.

sum: - Nvidia and Nike are among the latest companies to object to tokenized versions of their shares trading on the ICE-OKX venue, bringing the total to 50, according to Eleanor Terrett.
- The venture had initially proposed tokenizing shares from 62 companies.
- Objectors include Microsoft, Alphabet, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan, and the venue's notice gives no reasons for their objections.

A planned venue for trading tokenized U.S. stocks from New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) owner Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) and crypto exchange OKX has hit a wall, as Nvidia (NVDA) and Nike (NKE) joined a growing list of companies objecting to their shares being offered on it.

The number of companies objecting to OKXICE tokenizing their shares has grown to 50, journalist Eleanor Terrett said on X on Sunday. She said Nike, Costco (COST), Micron (MU), Reddit (RDDT) and Nvidia were among the new additions.
The venue's notice listed objectors including Microsoft (MSFT), Alphabet (GOOGL), Goldman Sachs (GS), JPMorgan (JPM), Broadcom (AVGO), Verizon (VZ), Intel (INTC) and Walmart (WMT).

AI-linked companies like CoreWeave (CRWV), Oracle (ORCL) and Arm Holdings (ARM) were also on it, along with CrowdStrike (CRWD), Corning (GLW), IREN (IREN) and Bloom Energy (BE). The objections piled up quickly. The venue's October 19 notice showed 16 objectors.

sum: A number of stocks jumped in the afternoon session after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller signaled support for holding interest rates steady amid emerging signs of disinflation.

During a Reuters NEXT Newsmaker interview, Governor Waller stated that if the positive economic trends seen over the last few months continue in the data due over the next two weeks, he would be inclined to support holding the federal funds target rate at its current setting. Waller pointed out that the three-month annualized inflation rate as measured by the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index has dropped from 4.76% in February to 3.05% currently, representing an encouraging downward trajectory.However, Waller warned that considerable uncertainty remains regarding how global conflicts, trade policy, and artificial intelligence will affect prices, according to Bloomberg. He cautioned that if upcoming August data shows this disinflationary progress has been fleeting, a rate hike may still be appropriate when the FOMC meets on September 15 and 16. Following Waller’s comments, market-implied odds for a September rate hike dropped to 48.4%, down 15 percentage points from the prior day, according to the CME Group’s FedWatch gauge cited by CNBC.

Intercontinental Exchange Invests in tZERO to Support Tokenized Securities Platform
sum: Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the owner of the New York Stock Exchange, has agreed to invest in tZERO as part of a collaboration to support its planned US tokenized securities platform.

ICE will participate in tZERO’s latest financing round, although the size of the investment has yet to be disclosed. It will also receive a license to use tZERO’s blockchain patent portfolio for the NYSE-affiliated platform and other potential applications.
The portfolio comprises 23 patent families and 103 patents covering areas including compliance controls, smart contracts, corporate actions and broker-dealer identity systems.

Under a memorandum of understanding, tZERO will act as a design partner for digital transfer agency and broker-dealer infrastructure. This technology is intended to support the on-chain settlement of tokenized securities traded through the platform.
ICE previously announced that the new market would support round-the-clock trading and immediate settlement of tokenized US-listed stocks and exchange-traded funds, subject to regulatory approval.
The platform is also expected to allow orders denominated in dollar amounts and support stablecoin-based funding.
“tZERO’s experience in regulated on-chain infrastructure makes them a valuable partner,” said Michael Blaugrund, vice president of strategic initiatives at ICE.
